rule: Docs code examples must use the correct Airflow API method name; use `.partition_key_pattern()` for regex filtering, not `.partition_key()` (exact-match).
trigger: diff adds a docs example calling `.partition_key(` with a regex string argument
rationale: The two methods have different semantics; using the wrong one in docs teaches users incorrect API usage and causes silent bugs.

evidence.excerpt: Switch the example to `.partition_key_pattern(...)` so the docs match the actual API.

rule: When documenting a new Airflow feature that was introduced in a specific version, give it a dedicated `.. note::` block or subheader rather than nesting it under an existing section that covers a different feature.
trigger: diff adds documentation for a new feature (e.g. Resumable Tasks) inside an existing section that already documents a distinct feature (e.g. Deferred Operators)
rationale: Users scanning docs may assume the nested feature was introduced at the same time as the parent section; a separate block makes the version scope unambiguous.

evidence.excerpt: Add another `..note` section or subheader for `concepts-resumable-tasks`.

rule: Derive `TASK_SDK_VERSION` from `PACKAGE_VERSION` using `packaging.version.parse_version()` (accessing `.minor` and `.micro`), never by splitting the version string on `.`.
trigger: diff introduces `PACKAGE_VERSION.split('.')` to derive TASK_SDK_VERSION or any component version
rationale: String splitting breaks for pre-release and local-version suffixes (e.g. `3.2.0.dev0`, `3.2.0+local`); `packaging.version` is already imported and handles all PEP 440 forms correctly.

rule: Auth manager docs must reference `get_url_refresh()` for the token-refresh endpoint path, not a hardcoded literal path such as `POST /auth/token/refresh`.
trigger: diff hardcodes an auth token refresh URL path in documentation instead of referencing the `get_url_refresh` method
rationale: Each auth manager may define its own refresh path; Airflow retrieves it via `get_url_refresh()`, so hardcoding a specific path is inaccurate and misleads implementors.

evidence.excerpt: Airflow can get this path with `get_url_refresh`; mention that method in the doc.

rule: Airflow docs must describe the current state of a feature without comparing to a previous version; do not use phrases like "no longer", "previously", or "as of version X".
trigger: diff adds text containing "no longer", "previously", "used to", or "as of Airflow X.Y" in documentation prose
rationale: Version-comparative language becomes stale and confusing; Airflow docs convention is to describe only the current behaviour.

evidence.excerpt: We always try to avoid comparing versions in docs, just mention how the state is.

rule: Document task-state-store and asset-state-store values as `JsonValue` (JSON-serialisable types), not as plain strings.
trigger: diff documents task store or asset store value types as "string" or "str" rather than `JsonValue` or JSON
rationale: Values are typed `JsonValue`; calling them plain strings will cause user confusion when they attempt to store dicts or integers.

evidence.excerpt: Values are `JsonValue` now; calling them strings will confuse users who try to store a dict or int.

rule: Public consumers of `XCOM_RETURN_KEY` (and other XCom constants) must import from the Task SDK's `BaseXCom`, not from `airflow.models.xcom`.
trigger: diff imports `XCOM_RETURN_KEY` or other XCom constants from `airflow.models.xcom` in user-facing code or docs
rationale: The constant was moved into `BaseXCom` in the Task SDK; `airflow.models.xcom` retains it only for internal `XComModel` usage and must not be promoted as the public import path.

evidence.excerpt: We should not recommend usage from `airflow.models.xcom`; it moved inside `BaseXcom` in task sdk.

rule: Docs about authentication must not present the FAB Auth Manager as the default; the default auth manager in Airflow 3 is the Simple Auth Manager.
trigger: diff adds documentation or configuration examples that imply FAB Auth Manager is used by default
rationale: FAB is no longer the default auth manager; presenting it as such leads operators to install unnecessary packages and misconfigure deployments.

evidence.excerpt: FAB Auth Manager is no longer the default; otherwise it uses the Simple Auth Manager.

rule: Getting-started / quickstart docs must document both the `uv`-based install path and the standard `pip` + `venv` path, not only one.
trigger: diff adds or rewrites the Airflow install quickstart section covering only a single tool (`uv` only or `pip` only)
rationale: Users may not have or want `uv`; the install guide should explain that `uv` is a faster alternative but also show the classic `venv + pip` approach.

evidence.excerpt: Both options — with `uv` and without (just with venv + pip) — should be explained there.

rule: Use a `bugfix.rst` newsfragment (not `significant.rst`) for non-user-facing internal fixes; omit the fragment entirely if the fix has no observable user impact.
trigger: diff adds a `significant.rst` newsfragment for an internal race-condition fix or scheduler-internal improvement with no API/behaviour change
rationale: Newsfragments are reserved for important and breaking changes; internal improvements bloat the changelog and dilute signal for operators.

evidence.excerpt: This is not user-facing but internal improvement; a bug newsfragment should be enough.
Newsfragments are for important and breaking changes only; please revert this.

rule: In newsfragments and release notes, capitalise "Dags" (title-case), not "DAGs" (all-caps).
trigger: diff in a newsfragment file contains the word "DAGs" (all-caps)
rationale: Consistent capitalisation across the changelog; the repo uses "Dags" as the standard form in release-note prose.

evidence.excerpt: Fix premature asset-triggered DagRuns … the scheduler now skips those Dags.

rule: Significant newsfragments about permission or endpoint changes must explicitly name the surface (e.g. "FastAPI UI `/dags` endpoint") to distinguish it from other endpoints with the same path.
trigger: diff adds a `significant.rst` newsfragment mentioning a `/dags` or other ambiguous endpoint without specifying whether it is the FastAPI UI route or a public REST API endpoint
rationale: Airflow exposes multiple `/dags` surfaces (UI vs public API); an ambiguous note misleads operators updating roles and may cause them to miss or over-apply permission changes.

evidence.excerpt: This change is specifically in the FastAPI UI route; clarify to reduce confusion for operators.

rule: Do not enable asyncio debug logging in production code paths or default configuration; it can expose credentials in task logs.
trigger: diff enables `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG`, `loop.set_debug(True)`, or asyncio debug logging in non-test production code
rationale: Airflow operators discovered that asyncio debug logging exposes credentials in task logs; the issue has been confirmed in production and remains in the backlog.

evidence.excerpt: We turned on asyncio debug logging and credentials were exposed in debug task logs.

rule: Do not add native/binary C-extension libraries as mandatory dependencies of `airflow-core`; they must be optional extras or provider-level dependencies.
trigger: diff adds a native library (e.g. one distributed as a compiled wheel with no pure-Python fallback) to the `dependencies` list in `airflow-core/pyproject.toml`
rationale: Native libraries are large and may fail to install on some OS/Python version combinations; making them required breaks `airflow-core` installation in those environments.

evidence.excerpt: It's a 2.4 MB native library; we do not want to make it a core requirement.

rule: In `BaseAuthManager` and its subclasses, `is_authorized_*` methods must accept `user: T` (the generic auth-user type-var) and represent multiple user IDs as `set[str]`; they must not accept concrete Airflow model types (e.g. `HITLUser`) as parameters.
trigger: diff adds or modifies an `is_authorized_*` method on an auth manager class that takes a concrete Airflow model type (e.g. `HITLUser`, `DagModel`) instead of `user: T` or primitive types
rationale: The base auth manager is generic and must not import or depend on concrete Airflow ORM models; doing so creates a circular or layering violation across the auth boundary.

evidence.excerpt: Not a big fan of having `HITLUser` as dependency of the base auth manager; only need the user ID.
